userPrompt: A running task can be paused and resumed. A Pause button beside Cancel stops the harness's run, leaving the task in the history as "Paused", its output, conversation, and starting snapshot kept. A paused task offers Resume, which carries on the same task, not a new one: it continues the task's conversation, telling the harness that its run was interrupted, that any step it was in the middle of may not have finished, and that files may have changed since, so it checks what it needs before carrying on from where it left off rather than starting over. The task's output continues beneath what it had, its time counts only while it runs, and its changed files and diff span the whole task, from the snapshot taken when it first started to the one taken when it finally ends. While a task is paused, its lane's queue carries on with the next prompt; a resumed task takes its place in the queue as a task sent at the time it was first sent. A paused Chain step resumes as that step, and the chain continues after it as ever. A task also pauses this way, rather than failing, when it stops because the harness's usage limit was reached.

content.content:
## Pausing

A running task can be paused and resumed. A Pause button, a small ghost button with a pause icon, whose tooltip says "Pause this task", sits beside Cancel wherever Cancel does, shown while the task is running. Pausing stops the harness's run, its process ended as cancelling ends it, and leaves the task in the history as "Paused": its output, its conversation, and the snapshot taken as it first started are kept, and nothing it changed is undone. A paused task is not under way: its lane is free, and its queue carries on with the next prompt, as after any task.
A paused task offers Resume, a small ghost button with a play icon, in place of Pause, wherever its actions are. Resume carries on the same task, never a new one: it is not saved in the history again and keeps its name. It carries on the task's own conversation, as the [HarnessIntegration](../../harness-integration/index.md#harness-integration) says, with a message telling the harness that its run was interrupted, that any step it was in the middle of may not have finished, and that files may have changed since, so it checks what it needs before carrying on from where it left off rather than starting over. The message is the application's own, from the [ModeSystemPrompts](../mode-system-prompts/index.md#mode-system-prompts), not the user's, and it is not compiled as a prompt; the spec is not built again ahead of it. A resumed task takes its place in its lane's queue as a task sent at the time it was first

### Sent

it runs as soon as its lane is free, ahead of every prompt sent

after it was first sent.
While it is paused, its status reads "Paused", its time stops, and it is listed among the previous tasks, or, for a chain step, with its chain. Once resumed, its output carries on beneath what it had, a muted row marking where it was paused and resumed, its time counts on from where it stopped, counting only while it runs, and its changed files and their diffs span the whole task, from the snapshot taken when it first started to the one taken when it finally ends. It can be paused and resumed any number of times, and cancelled while paused, which ends it as Cancelled. A paused task whose conversation can no longer be carried on resumes as a new conversation, as the [HarnessIntegration](../../harness-integration/index.md#harness-integration) says, told the task's prompt and its output so far.
A paused Chain step resumes as that step, and the chain carries on after it as ever, its next step sent once it finishes. While one of its steps is paused and none runs, the chain reads Paused.
A task also pauses this way, rather than failing, when it stops because the harness's usage limit was reached, as the harness says in its result or its errors: it reads "Paused" with a muted note saying the usage limit was reached and when it resets, if the harness says, and waits to be resumed by hand. Paused tasks are kept across restarts and can be resumed after one.

## Resuming

The resume prompt is the message given to a paused task when it is resumed, as the [PromptSending](../sending/index.md#prompt-sending) says, sent on its own as the next message of the task's conversation, never compiled as a prompt. Like the injected prompts, each project has its own, saved with its data in resume.md beside the templates, and edited in the [SettingsWindow](../../settings-window/index.md#settings-window); with no file yet the project uses its default, which says:
Your previous run on this task was interrupted before it finished. Any step you were in the middle of, such as an edit, a command, or a build, may not have completed, and files may have changed since. Before carrying on, check the state of what you were working on: re-read the files you were changing and re-run any check you need. Then carry on from where you left off; don't start the task over or redo work that is already done.

## Saving

input.message:
Map of a task run's lifecycle. All paths are under /home/hyphyphyph/piton/repl. Line numbers are for src/prompt_mode.rs unless another file is named.

## 1. `fn start(&mut self, text: String, sending: Sending, cx)`, lines 5772-6788
- `enum Sending` (257): `Now(SendMode, Attached, bool sliced, Option<CodeTask>, Option<String> sent_from, bool post_build_update, Option<String> named_after)` or `Queued(QueuedPrompt)`.
- 5778 `let task_ix = self.push_task(text.clone().into(), cx);` (push_task is at 3318). 5780-5781 set `goes_on = true` and `ran_here = true`.
- 5784-5789 `chain_stamp`: the queued file's stamp, else `self.next_chain_stamp.take()`, else `prompt_queue::stamp()`.
- 5791 `queued_at` is kept for the debug log.
- **5796 `self.tasks[task_ix].started = Some(SystemTime::now());`**
- 5846 `let lanes = Lanes::of(mode)`. 5849 `let lane = conversation_lane(mode)`. **5850 `self.working = self.working.with(lanes, true);`**, then `chat_input.set_busy(working)`.
- 5860-5863 `new_conversation`. 5871-5880 `let resume = Session::resume(self.session.of(lane), &project_dir).filter(!new_conversation).filter(in_container matches)`. 5881 `let epoch = *self.session_epoch.of(lane);`
- 5895 sets `status = Building` if `builds` (`builds` = not Ask and not Freeform).
- 5902-5922: Cancel setup (see section 2).
- 5923 `build = cx.background_spawn(piton_build::build(..))`.
- 5932-5947 `system` is a background job: `hidden_anchor::project_system_prompt_for(system_mode, &project_dir)`. Freeform uses `conversation_system` instead.
- 5948-6034 `compile` closure:
  - `Queued`: `prompt_queue::remove` first.
  - `Now`: `resolve_anchor`.
  - Then `hidden_anchor::save(&anchor,..)` gives the history `file`. At 6012 it returns early with no compile if cancelled. Otherwise it calls `hidden_anchor::compile`.
- **6036 the big closure: `self._pending[lane_slot(lanes)] = cx.spawn(async move |this, cx| { ... })`.** `_pending: [Task<()>; 2]`, one per lane (1954/2181).
  - 6038 `phases = debug_log::Phases::new(&project_dir, known)`. 6040 `phases.since("queued", ..)`.
  - 6043-6069 phase "spec build", raced with `until_cancelled()`. Status goes Building to Compiling.
  - 6094-6117 naming, raced with `until_cancelled()`, then `phases.rename`.
  - 6118 `compile`. 6121 `let mut record = RunRecord::default(); let mut prompt_file = None; let mut finished = None;`
  - 6133-6138: cancelled before running gives `Ok(None)`, so it never runs.
  - 6141 is the `Ok(Some((anchor, compiled, imported)))` arm:
    - `record.user_prompt`, model and effort.
    - `understanding_file`, `message = system_prompts::with_instructions(..)` (6171), `sent_system = system.await` (6173).
    - `record.sent_to(agent, ..)`, `record.resumed`, `record.resumed_from = resume.clone()` (6178-6181).
    - `protected = harness::Protected { root: told_off, unread, container, model, effort, files, session_copy: prompt_file.with_extension("session") }` (6226-6237).
  - 6241-6254 phase "snapshot": `snapshot_before = task_snapshot::take(&dir, &name, "before")`, then `record.snapshot_before = ...`.
  - **6258-6278 the harness call:**
    ```rust
    let harness::Run { mut events, feed, stop } = {
        phases.begin("harness"); phases.begin("first event");
        harness::send_task(message, sent_system.clone(), compiled.images.clone(),
            resume.clone().map(|session| harness::Resume { session, fork: false }),
            project_dir.clone(), protected) };
    ```
  - 6279-6327, in `this.update`:
    - `usage.start_run(usage_conversation(lane), epoch, RunKind::Task, resume)` gives `usage_run`.
    - `task.feed = feed`, then **`cancel.stop = Some(stop.clone())`** (6300).
    - `if is_cancelled() { stop.stop() }` (6303).
    - It also starts the understanding watch, sets `task.given`, and calls `show_compiled`.
  - 6333-6419: the event loop (see section 2 and section 4).
  - 6421-6428 `usage.end_run`. 6433-6505: a Spec container run gets a host `piton build` afterwards, with status set to `Building` temporarily, and possibly `spec_fix_due`. 6509-6534: the told-off notice.
- harness signatures, all in src/harness.rs:
  - `pub fn send_task(prompt, system_prompt: Option<String>, images: Vec<PathBuf>, resume: Option<Resume>, project_dir: PathBuf, protected: Protected) -> Run` (277).
  - `pub struct Run { events: mpsc::UnboundedReceiver<HarnessEvent>, feed: Option<Feed>, stop: Stop }` (265).
  - `Resume { session: String, fork: bool }` (174).
  - `Protected` (201).
  - `Stop(Arc<Mutex<Stopping>>)` (420), with `stop()` at 445 (closes the feed, kills the child, and a run not yet started never starts) and `is_stopped()`.

## 2. Cancellation
- `struct Cancel { cancelled: Arc<AtomicBool>, signal: Option<oneshot::Sender<()>>, stop: Option<harness::Stop> }` (427-434). `Cancel::cancel()` (437-445) stores true, calls `stop.stop()`, and sends on the signal.
- `fn cancel_task(&mut self, ix, cx)` (3779-3788): checks `task.can_cancel()`, which is `status.is_active() && cancel.is_some()` (825). Then it calls `task.cancel()`, which is `PromptTask::cancel` (817-822: `status = Cancelled; subagents.end(); reply.cancel(); stamp_end()`), then `task.cancel.as_mut().cancel()`, then `cx.notify()`.
- In `start` (5902-5922):
  - `cancelled = Arc<AtomicBool>` and `(signal, on_cancel) = oneshot::channel()`. `task.cancel = Some(Cancel{.., stop: None})`, and `on_cancel.shared()`.
  - `until_cancelled = move || async { if on_cancel.await.is_err() { pending().await } }`. This resolves only when cancelled.
  - `is_cancelled = move || cancelled.load(SeqCst)`.
- Where cancellation is noticed:
  - The build and naming selects (6048, 6096).
  - The `cancelled.load` check in compile (6012).
  - 6133-6138.
  - 6303, where the stop is installed late.
  - The event loop at 6337-6346: `select(events.next(), until_cancelled())`. Either the stream ending or cancellation causes a `break`.
  - 6349-6358: after cancellation, `Failed`, `Finished` and `Answered` are ignored (`continue`).
- `fail()` (806) never overwrites `Cancelled`. `end_run()` (837) keeps a Cancelled task cancelled.
- `TaskStatus` (513-531): Building, Compiling, Preparing, Running, Done, Failed, Cancelled, Unrecorded, Stopped. `is_active()` covers Building, Compiling, Preparing and Running.

## 3. End-of-run block (6535-6787)
- 6535 `phases.end("harness", if is_cancelled() {"cancelled"} else {"ended"})`.
- 6538-6582 "closing snapshot": if `snapshot_before` is set, `phases.begin("closing snapshot")`, get edited paths, then in the background `task_snapshot::take(&dir, &snapshot_name, "after")` and `ChangedFiles::read(repo_top, before, after, &edited)`. Then `phases.end(.., "taken"/"failed")`, `record.snapshot_after = after`, and **`task.changed = changed`**. `ChangedFiles::read` is at 401.
- 6585-6592: if resumed but no `Session` event arrived (`!started`) and the run was not cancelled, it calls `Session::forget`.
- 6596-6614: `Session::finished(this.session.of_mut(lane), id, run_context, ..)` when the epoch matches, then sets `in_container`.
- 6616-6627: the `Err` arm sets `record.error` and calls `task.fail`.
- 6630 `record.cancelled = is_cancelled();` 6631 `record.phases = phases.close(...)`.
- 6633-6645: `record.started_at` / `ended_at` via `to_millis` (8821) from `task.started` / `task.ended`. `ended_at` falls back to now.
- 6648-6659 `record.marked_done`. **6660 `let record_file = prompt_file.clone();`** 6663-6674: background job that extends `sent_prompts` and calls **`prompt_history::save_record(&file, &record)`**.
- 6676 final `this.update`:
  - `task.feed = None; task.cancel = None; task.end();` (6682-6684).
  - Re-save of marked_done via `record_file` (6685-6694), and an error notice if saving failed.
  - **6703 `this.working = this.working.with(lanes, false);`**, then `load_history` if `history_stale`, then `set_busy`.
  - 6715-6724 `add_commit_note` when Done and not cancelled.
  - 6730-6760 chain logic: `done`, `fix_due` (from `spec_fix_due`) leads to `spec_fix`. Otherwise `release_held_chain` (6793), or `chain_next(task)` (defined at 8690) with `task.chain_stamp`, or `next_added_step`.
  - **6765-6782 `cx.defer(...)`**: calls `chain_on(text, sending, chain_stamp)` (6816), `send_added_step`, sets `task.goes_on = false`, then **`this.auto_send_next(cx)`**.
- `PromptTask::end()` (831) = `end_run(); settle_outcome(); stamp_end();`. `end_run` gives a "The harness stopped without a result." failure unless the task is done or cancelled.
- Debug-log phases appear in this order: "queued", "spec build", "snapshot", "harness", "first event", then `phases.follow(&event)` (6360), "closing snapshot", and finally `close("cancelled"|"ended")`. `debug_log::Phases` is at src/debug_log.rs:173; its methods `new/rename/begin/end/since/close/follow` are at 192-289.
- Questions (Ask) run a parallel copy at about 6993-7140. It uses `AskLog`, which saves on Drop (991-1019), and `harness::Resume { session, fork }` at 7081.

## 4. Session tracking
- `struct Session { project_dir, in_container: Option<bool>, id: String, context: Option<u64>, system_prompt: Option<String> }` (1024).
- Its functions:
  - `resume` (1040)
  - `forget` (1049)
  - `latest` (from history)
  - `finished` (1089)
  - `follow(session, current: bool, run: &mut Option<String>, event, project_dir, sent) -> Option<String>` (1116, `#[must_use]`). It returns a "left" id.
- Fields: `session: PerLane<Option<Session>>` and `session_epoch: PerLane<u64>`. `PerLane<T>{code, spec}` has `of` and `of_mut(lane)` (8597-8617). `conversation_lane(mode)` is at 8621 and `lane_slot` at 8659.
- In the loop (6328-6411):
  - `let mut started = false; let mut run_session = None; let mut run_context = None;`
  - `HarnessEvent::Session(_)` sets `started = true`.
  - `NewConversation(lost)` calls `Session::forget` + `keep_left` and sets `task.new_conversation`.
  - `Session::follow(this.session.of_mut(lane), *this.session_epoch.of(lane) == epoch, &mut run_session, &event, ..)`.
  - Then `this.apply_event(task_ix, event, cx)`.
- `PromptTask::apply_event` (781) also sets `task.session` from `HarnessEvent::Session`.
- The resume value is computed at 5871 and passed as `harness::Resume{session, fork:false}` at 6271.

## 5. Elapsed time
- Fields (361-369): `started: Option<SystemTime>`, `ended: Option<SystemTime>`, `estimated: Option<(SystemTime, SystemTime)>`, all initialized to None at 611-613.
- `started` is set only at 5796 in `start`, and from the history at 679.
- `stamp_end()` (725): if `started.is_some() && !status.is_active() && ended.is_none()`, then `ended = now`. It is called from `apply` (721), `fail`, `cancel` and `end`.
- `span()` (733) returns `(started, ended, approximate)`, falling back to `estimated`.
- `took()` (743) returns a `Took{time, approximate}`. It measures up to now while active, and returns None if the task is inactive with no end.
- `chain_took` is around 1491, and `took_label` is at 1510.
- To support a pause, you will need to account for paused intervals here. Nothing tracks them today.

## 6. Queue
- `enum QueuePlace { End, Head, ChainSentAt(u128) }` (162). `struct QueueItem { id, text, saved: Option<QueuedPrompt>, wait, sent_from, images, files, new_conversation, mode, queued_at: u128 }` (174).
- `auto_send_next` (4344): `if self.auto_send && !self.queue_held { while self.send_next(cx) {} }`.
- `enqueue` (about 4357) calls `enqueue_at(QueuePlace::End, ..)`. `enqueue_at` (4388-4500) computes `(queued_at, at)` per place, inserts the `QueueItem`, then saves in the background via `prompt_queue::add_at`, then `queue_saved` (4502), which calls `auto_send_next` unless `wait`.
- `chain_holds(lanes, stamp)` (4822). `next_sendable()` (4836-4858) walks the queue with `held = self.working`. An item is ready when it is saved, not being edited, not held by `tasks_tab`, and `!chain_holds`. It returns the item if `!held.overlaps(lanes)`, otherwise adds `held = held.with(lanes, true)`.
- `send_next` (4862) removes the item and calls `self.start(item.text, Sending::Queued(saved), cx)`. `send_next_clicked` clears `queue_held`.
- `chain_on` (6816) starts at once if `!self.working.queues(mode) && !earlier_waits`, setting `next_chain_stamp`. Otherwise it calls `enqueue_at(ChainSentAt(stamp) | Head)`.
- `Lanes` is in src/chat_input.rs:456: `{code, spec}` with `NONE`, `ALL`, `only`, `of(mode)` (Ask gives NONE, Freeform gives ALL), `overlaps`, `with(other, busy)` and `queues(mode)`. `Lane` is `{Code, Spec}` (449).
- `working: Lanes` is a field of PromptMode (2092) and of ProjectSession (1945).

## 7. Restore from history
- `PromptTask::restore` (621) is `#[cfg(test)]` and just calls `restore_in(saved, None)`.
- The real one is `restore_in(saved, project_dir)` (628). It reads the snapshots, calls `restore_replayed`, then `ChangedFiles::read`. It is called from `load_history` (4275, used at 4305) and from the asks load (5735).
- `restore_replayed` (645-707):
  - Builds the anchor fields.
  - A missing record, or `holds_only_the_mark()`, gives `reply.stop()` and `Unrecorded`.
  - `started_at`/`ended_at` go through `from_millis` (8816). Without them it uses `estimated` from `sent_at` and `recorded_at`.
  - Sets `given`, compiled `user_prompt`, and replays `record.events()` through `task.apply`.
  - `if record.cancelled { task.cancel() } else if let Some(error) { apply(Failed(error)) }`, then `task.end()`.
- src/prompt_history.rs:
  - `RunRecord` (25, serde camelCase) has fields `user_prompt`, `harness`, `system_prompt`, `instructions`, `resumed`, `resumed_from`, `output: Vec<Value>`, `error: Option<String>` (62), `cancelled: bool` (65), `marked_done`, `picked`, `sent_prompts`, `started_at: Option<u64>` (83, millis), `ended_at` (86), `phases: Vec<Phase>` (91), `snapshot_before` (96) and `snapshot_after` (100).
  - Its methods are `sent_to` (116), `holds_only_the_mark` (123), `harness()` (132), `note(&event)` (139; `Failed` sets `error`, `NewConversation` clears output, `resumed` and `resumed_from`) and `events()` (164).
  - `SavedPrompt { anchor, text, record, sent_at, recorded_at }` (190).
  - `save_record(prompt_file, record)` (207) writes `prompt_file.with_extension("json")` as pretty JSON. `save_marked_done` is at 217, and `load`/`load_asks` at 310/316.
- To add a "paused" state, you would need a new serde field on `RunRecord` and handling in `restore_replayed`.

## 8. Usage-limit detection
- Nothing parses "usage limit", "limit reached" or "hit your limit" text. Only structured rate-limit events are parsed:
  - src/harness.rs:2212: `Some("rate_limit_event")` gives `HarnessEvent::Limits(claude_limits(&event["rate_limit_info"]))`.
  - `claude_limits` (2365-2397) reads `unifiedWindows.*.{utilization, resetsAt}`, or a single `rateLimitType` with `utilization`. A `status == "rejected"` without utilization becomes `used = 1.0`.
  - The variant `HarnessEvent::Limits(Vec<PlanLimit>)` is at 132. Tests are at 2676-2722 (statuses "allowed", "allowed_warning", "rejected").
- src/usage.rs:
  - `PlanLimit { name, used: f64, resets_at: Option<u64> }` (221), with `label()`, `percent()` and `reset_by(now)` (256).
  - `PlanLimits { reported: Vec<(Agent, Vec<PlanLimit>, u64)> }` (745), with `follow(agent, event, now)` (752).
- prompt_mode `follow_usage` (5544) calls `self.usage.follow` and `self.limits.follow(agent, event, now)`. It is called from the run loop at 6378.
- Error results come through `HarnessEvent::Finished { is_error, result }`. That is parsed at harness.rs:2272, where `result` falls back to the joined `errors` array. A text match for limit messages would have to go there or in the run loop.

## 9. System prompts
- src/system_prompts.rs:
  - `const DIR = "system-prompts"` (87).
  - `enum Prompt { System, Mode(SendMode), SpecReading, CodeToSpec, SpecToCode }` (95), with `ALL: [Prompt; 8]` (106), `key()` (118), `label()` (129) and `From<SendMode>`.

  - The build and naming selects (6048, 6096).

  - 6133-6138.

- `chain_took` is around 1491, and `took_label` is at 1510.
- To support a pause, you will need to account for paused intervals here. Nothing tracks them today.

  - 6596-6614: `Session::finished(this.session.of_mut(lane), id, run_context, ..)` when the epoch matches, then sets `in_container`.
  - 6616-6627: the `Err` arm sets `record.error` and calls `task.fail`.
  - 6630 `record.cancelled = is_cancelled();` 6631 `record.phases = phases.close(...)`.
  - 6633-6645: `record.started_at` / `ended_at` via `to_millis` (8821) from `task.started` / `task.ended`. `ended_at` falls back to now.
  - 6648-6659 `record.marked_done`. **6660 `let record_file = prompt_file.clone();`** 6663-6674: background job that extends `sent_prompts` and calls **`prompt_history::save_record(&file, &record)`**.
  - 6676 final `this.update`:
    - `task.feed = None; task.cancel = None; task.end();` (6682-6684).
    - Re-save of marked_done via `record_file` (6685-6694), and an error notice if saving failed.
    - **6703 `this.working = this.working.with(lanes, false);`**, then `load_history` if `history_stale`, then `set_busy`.
    - 6715-6724 `add_commit_note` when Done and not cancelled.
    - 6730-6760 chain logic: `done`, `fix_due` (from `spec_fix_due`) leads to `spec_fix`. Otherwise `release_held_chain` (6793), or `chain_next(task)` (defined at 8690) with `task.chain_stamp`, or `next_added_step`.
    - **6765-6782 `cx.defer(...)`**: calls `chain_on(text, sending, chain_stamp)` (6816), `send_added_step`, sets `task.goes_on = false`, then **`this.auto_send_next(cx)`**.
  - `PromptTask::end()` (831) = `end_run(); settle_outcome(); stamp_end();`. `end_run` gives a "The harness stopped without a result." failure unless the task is done or cancelled.
  - Debug-log phases appear in this order: "queued", "spec build", "snapshot", "harness", "first event", then `phases.follow(&event)` (6360), "closing snapshot", and finally `close("cancelled"|"ended")`. `debug_log::Phases` is at src/debug_log.rs:173; its methods `new/rename/begin/end/since/close/follow` are at 192-289.
  - Questions (Ask) run a parallel copy at about 6993-7140. It uses `AskLog`, which saves on Drop (991-1019), and `harness::Resume { session, fork }` at 7081.
  
  ## 4. Session tracking
  - `struct Session { project_dir, in_container: Option<bool>, id: String, context: Option<u64>, system_prompt: Option<String> }` (1024).
  - Its functions:
    - `resume` (1040)
    - `forget` (1049)
    - `latest` (from history)
    - `finished` (1089)
    - `follow(session, current: bool, run: &mut Option<String>, event, project_dir, sent) -> Option<String>` (1116, `#[must_use]`). It returns a "left" id.
  - Fields: `session: PerLane<Option<Session>>` and `session_epoch: PerLane<u64>`. `PerLane<T>{code, spec}` has `of` and `of_mut(lane)` (8597-8617). `conversation_lane(mode)` is at 8621 and `lane_slot` at 8659.
  - In the loop (6328-6411):
    - `let mut started = false; let mut run_session = None; let mut run_context = None;`
    - `HarnessEvent::Session(_)` sets `started = true`.
    - `NewConversation(lost)` calls `Session::forget` + `keep_left` and sets `task.new_conversation`.
    - `Session::follow(this.session.of_mut(lane), *this.session_epoch.of(lane) == epoch, &mut run_session, &event, ..)`.
    - Then `this.apply_event(task_ix, event, cx)`.
  - `PromptTask::apply_event` (781) also sets `task.session` from `HarnessEvent::Session`.
  - The resume value is computed at 5871 and passed as `harness::Resume{session, fork:false}` at 6271.
  
  ## 5. Elapsed time
  - Fields (361-369): `started: Option<SystemTime>`, `ended: Option<SystemTime>`, `estimated: Option<(SystemTime, SystemTime)>`, all initialized to None at 611-613.
  - `started` is set only at 5796 in `start`, and from the history at 679.
  - `stamp_end()` (725): if `started.is_some() && !status.is_active() && ended.is_none()`, then `ended = now`. It is called from `apply` (721), `fail`, `cancel` and `end`.
  - `span()` (733) returns `(started, ended, approximate)`, falling back to `estimated`.
  - `took()` (743) returns a `Took{time, approximate}`. It measures up to now while active, and returns None if the task is inactive with no end.
  - `chain_took` is around 1491, and `took_label` is at 1510.
  - To support a pause, you will need to account for paused intervals here. Nothing tracks them today.
  
  ## 6. Queue
  - `enum QueuePlace { End, Head, ChainSentAt(u128) }` (162). `struct QueueItem { id, text, saved: Option<QueuedPrompt>, wait, sent_from, images, files, new_conversation, mode, queued_at: u128 }` (174).
  - `auto_send_next` (4344): `if self.auto_send && !self.queue_held { while self.send_next(cx) {} }`.
  - `enqueue` (about 4357) calls `enqueue_at(QueuePlace::End, ..)`. `enqueue_at` (4388-4500) computes `(queued_at, at)` per place, inserts the `QueueItem`, then saves in the background via `prompt_queue::add_at`, then `queue_saved` (4502), which calls `auto_send_next` unless `wait`.
  - `chain_holds(lanes, stamp)` (4822). `next_sendable()` (4836-4858) walks the queue with `held = self.working`. An item is ready when it is saved, not being edited, not held by `tasks_tab`, and `!chain_holds`. It returns the item if `!held.overlaps(lanes)`, otherwise adds `held = held.with(lanes, true)`.
  - `send_next` (4862) removes the item and calls `self.start(item.text, Sending::Queued(saved), cx)`. `send_next_clicked` clears `queue_held`.
  - `chain_on` (6816) starts at once if `!self.working.queues(mode) && !earlier_waits`, setting `next_chain_stamp`. Otherwise it calls `enqueue_at(ChainSentAt(stamp) | Head)`.
  - `Lanes` is in src/chat_input.rs:456: `{code, spec}` with `NONE`, `ALL`, `only`, `of(mode)` (Ask gives NONE, Freeform gives ALL), `overlaps`, `with(other, busy)` and `queues(mode)`. `Lane` is `{Code, Spec}` (449).
  - `working: Lanes` is a field of PromptMode (2092) and of ProjectSession (1945).
  
  ## 7. Restore from history
  - `PromptTask::restore` (621) is `#[cfg(test)]` and just calls `restore_in(saved, None)`.
  - The real one is `restore_in(saved, project_dir)` (628). It reads the snapshots, calls `restore_replayed`, then `ChangedFiles::read`. It is called from `load_history` (4275, used at 4305) and from the asks load (5735).
  - `restore_replayed` (645-707):
    - Builds the anchor fields.
    - A missing record, or `holds_only_the_mark()`, gives `reply.stop()` and `Unrecorded`.
    - `started_at`/`ended_at` go through `from_millis` (8816). Without them it uses `estimated` from `sent_at` and `recorded_at`.
    - Sets `given`, compiled `user_prompt`, and replays `record.events()` through `task.apply`.
    - `if record.cancelled { task.cancel() } else if let Some(error) { apply(Failed(error)) }`, then `task.end()`.
  - src/prompt_history.rs:
    - `RunRecord` (25, serde camelCase) has fields `user_prompt`, `harness`, `system_prompt`, `instructions`, `resumed`, `resumed_from`, `output: Vec<Value>`, `error: Option<String>` (62), `cancelled: bool` (65), `marked_done`, `picked`, `sent_prompts`, `started_at: Option<u64>` (83, millis), `ended_at` (86), `phases: Vec<Phase>` (91), `snapshot_before` (96) and `snapshot_after` (100).
    - Its methods are `sent_to` (116), `holds_only_the_mark` (123), `harness()` (132), `note(&event)` (139; `Failed` sets `error`, `NewConversation` clears output, `resumed` and `resumed_from`) and `events()` (164).
    - `SavedPrompt { anchor, text, record, sent_at, recorded_at }` (190).
    - `save_record(prompt_file, record)` (207) writes `prompt_file.with_extension("json")` as pretty JSON. `save_marked_done` is at 217, and `load`/`load_asks` at 310/316.
  - To add a "paused" state, you would need a new serde field on `RunRecord` and handling in `restore_replayed`.
  
  ## 8. Usage-limit detection
  - Nothing parses "usage limit", "limit reached" or "hit your limit" text. Only structured rate-limit events are parsed:
    - src/harness.rs:2212: `Some("rate_limit_event")` gives `HarnessEvent::Limits(claude_limits(&event["rate_limit_info"]))`.
    - `claude_limits` (2365-2397) reads `unifiedWindows.*.{utilization, resetsAt}`, or a single `rateLimitType` with `utilization`. A `status == "rejected"` without utilization becomes `used = 1.0`.
    - The variant `HarnessEvent::Limits(Vec<PlanLimit>)` is at 132. Tests are at 2676-2722 (statuses "allowed", "allowed_warning", "rejected").
  - src/usage.rs:
    - `PlanLimit { name, used: f64, resets_at: Option<u64> }` (221), with `label()`, `percent()` and `reset_by(now)` (256).
    - `PlanLimits { reported: Vec<(Agent, Vec<PlanLimit>, u64)> }` (745), with `follow(agent, event, now)` (752).
  - prompt_mode `follow_usage` (5544) calls `self.usage.follow` and `self.limits.follow(agent, event, now)`. It is called from the run loop at 6378.
  - Error results come through `HarnessEvent::Finished { is_error, result }`. That is parsed at harness.rs:2272, where `result` falls back to the joined `errors` array. A text match for limit messages would have to go there or in the run loop.
  
  ## 9. System prompts
  - src/system_prompts.rs:
    - `const DIR = "system-prompts"` (87).
    - `enum Prompt { System, Mode(SendMode), SpecReading, CodeToSpec, SpecToCode }` (95), with `ALL: [Prompt; 8]` (106), `key()` (118), `label()` (129) and `From<SendMode>`.
    - `default_prompt(prompt)` (149-175) uses a `baked!` macro: `include_str!(concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), "/.suspense/system-prompts/", $key, ".md"))`. The keys are system, code, combined, spec, ask, spec-reading, code-to-spec and spec-to-code. Freeform is "". The result is `.trim_end()`ed.
    - `ask_cards()` (69) includes `.suspense/system-prompts/ask-cards.md` the same way.
    - `dir(project_dir)` = `project_dir/APP_DIR/system-prompts` (178). `file()` is at 183.
    - `load` (189) reads the file trimmed, and on NotFound returns `default_prompt`.
    - `save` (200). `save_missing(project_dir)` (210) writes the default for each `Prompt::ALL` with no file. It is called at prompt_mode.rs:8422 and settings_window.rs:414.
    - `project_system_prompt` (339). `with_instructions` (444).
  - src/hidden_anchor.rs:1233 `project_system_prompt_for(mode, dir)` loads `Prompt::System` and `SpecReading`.
  - The repo-root `.suspense/system-prompts/` holds ask-cards.md, ask.md, code.md, code-to-spec.md, combined.md, spec.md, spec-reading.md, spec-to-code.md, suspense-fluency.md and system.md.
  - These .md defaults are baked with `include_str!`, not by build.rs. build.rs `compile_prompts()` (163-200) is a separate mechanism for a different folder: it compiles `system-prompts/*.pi` (Piton, a repo-root folder outside `.suspense`) with `piton`, falling back to the `system-prompts/compiled.json` snapshot. It generates `$OUT_DIR/baked_prompts.rs` modules/constants, which src/baked_prompts.rs `include!`s, plus `fill(template, values)` for `<name>` placeholders. Examples are `divergence::INTRO` and `commit_note::REQUEST`.
  
  ## Notes for pause/resume
  - `Cancel` is the only control handle stored on the task. `Stop` kills the process, so "pausing" a running harness means stopping it and resuming via `harness::Resume { session: run_session, fork: false }`.
  - `task.session` and `run_session` hold the id to resume. `Protected.session_copy` keeps a `.session` copy beside the record.
  - The lane is freed at 6703 and the queue continues at 6778, so a paused task would need to either keep `working` set for its lanes or let the queue proceed.

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   Every user turn is a "second step of a chain" prompt. Each one requires:
   - Change the code in ./src to match the compiled spec in .claude/reference.
   - Never read or change ./spec (a deny rule exists).
   - Write the constraints list once, before the first change, to the named .suspense/history/<id>.understanding.md file: at most 12 lines, each linking to a reference file.
   - End with a short reply of a few sentences.
   - Where the spec and the prompt disagree, follow the spec and say so.

   The current request, verbatim:
   "A running task can be paused and resumed. A Pause button beside Cancel stops the harness's run, leaving the task in the history as "Paused", its output, conversation, and starting snapshot kept. A paused task offers Resume, which carries on the same task, not a new one: it continues the task's conversation, telling the harness that its run was interrupted, that any step it was in the middle of may not have finished, and that files may have changed since, so it checks what it needs before carrying on from where it left off rather than starting over. The task's output continues beneath what it had, its time counts only while it runs, and its changed files and diff span the whole task, from the snapshot taken when it first started to the one taken when it finally ends. While a task is paused, its lane's queue carries on with the next prompt; a resumed task takes its place in the queue as a task sent at the time it was first sent. A paused Chain step resumes as that step, and the chain continues after it as ever. A task also pauses this way, rather than failing, when it stops because the harness's usage limit was reached."

   The spec step's anchors for it:
   - `PromptSending` `#pausing` and `#cancelling`
   - `MessageList` `#status` and `#buttons`
   - `ModeSystemPrompts` `#resuming`
   - `PromptEditor` `#chained-tasks`

   - `ProjectData` `#contents`: resume.md lives in system-prompts.

2. Key Technical Concepts:

a='''    fn cancel_project(
        name: &str,'''
assert a in s
s=s.replace(a,'''    /// Held by each test whose harness runs are stopped mid-turn, one at a
    /// time: stopping one's harness while another's runs wakes its run from
    /// outside its test's scheduler.
    static STOPPING_RUNS: std::sync::Mutex<()> = std::sync::Mutex::new(());

'''+a,1)
for name in ["async fn cancelling_a_run_keeps_its_output_and_the_queue_carries_on(cx: &mut TestAppContext) {","async fn pausing_a_run_and_resuming_it_carries_on_the_same_task(cx: &mut TestAppContext) {"]:
    assert name in s
    s=s.replace(name,name+"\n        let _one_at_a_time = STOPPING_RUNS.lock().unwrap_or_else(|poisoned| poisoned.into_inner());",1)
open('src/prompt_mode.rs','w').write(s)
EOF

content.text:
Pause and resume now work, and the build is clean. The new test passes, run both alone and with the full `prompt_mode` tests (three times in a row). The full suite still has failures that don't come from this change; details below.

**What it does:**
- **Pause:** a running task's header gets a Pause button beside Stop, and its Tasks tab details get one beside Cancel. Pausing stops the harness's run like cancelling does, but the task reads "Paused" in the warning colour. Its output, conversation and starting snapshot are all kept. Its lane is freed, so the queue moves on to the next prompt.
- **Resume:** a paused task shows Resume instead, and can still be cancelled. Resume carries on the same task, not a new one:
  - It sends `resume.md` (now in the project's system prompts, with the spec's default text) as the next message in the task's own conversation. Nothing is compiled and the spec isn't rebuilt.
  - Its output continues beneath "Resumed".
  - Its time doesn't count while paused.
  - Its changed files and diff run from the snapshot taken when it first started.
  - If its lane is busy, it waits and goes ahead of prompts queued after it was first sent.
- **Chains:** a paused chain step doesn't hand on to the next step. Once resumed and finished, the chain continues as normal. A chain with a paused step and nothing running reads "Paused".
- **Usage limit:** if the harness stops because its usage limit was reached, the task pauses instead of failing, with a note saying when the limit resets (when the harness has reported that).
- **Restarts:** the paused state and paused time are saved in the history record, so a paused task can still be resumed after a restart.

**Where I went beyond the prompt, following the spec:** if a paused task's conversation can't be carried on, it resumes in a new conversation. That message includes its original prompt and its output so far, followed by the resume prompt. I also added the resume prompt to the settings window's injected prompts.

**Test fixes:**
- The new test and the existing `cancelling` test both start real harness runs. They failed in the full suite because neither called `allow_parking()`, which the other harness-run tests use; I added it to both.
- A finished run now drops its event stream straight away.
- I updated the system-prompt and settings tests for the new Resume prompt.

**Still failing, not caused by this change:**

- `long_output_is_measured_a_few_rows_a_frame` fails sometimes when run with the other tests. It also failed with my test switched off, and passes on its own.

output.result:
Pause and resume now work, and the build is clean. The new test passes, run both alone and with the full `prompt_mode` tests (three times in a row). The full suite still has failures that don't come from this change; details below.

**What it does:**
- **Pause:** a running task's header gets a Pause button beside Stop, and its Tasks tab details get one beside Cancel. Pausing stops the harness's run like cancelling does, but the task reads "Paused" in the warning colour. Its output, conversation and starting snapshot are all kept. Its lane is freed, so the queue moves on to the next prompt.
- **Resume:** a paused task shows Resume instead, and can still be cancelled. Resume carries on the same task, not a new one:
  - It sends `resume.md` (now in the project's system prompts, with the spec's default text) as the next message in the task's own conversation. Nothing is compiled and the spec isn't rebuilt.
  - Its output continues beneath "Resumed".
  - Its time doesn't count while paused.
  - Its changed files and diff run from the snapshot taken when it first started.
  - If its lane is busy, it waits and goes ahead of prompts queued after it was first sent.
- **Chains:** a paused chain step doesn't hand on to the next step. Once resumed and finished, the chain continues as normal. A chain with a paused step and nothing running reads "Paused".
- **Usage limit:** if the harness stops because its usage limit was reached, the task pauses instead of failing, with a note saying when the limit resets (when the harness has reported that).
- **Restarts:** the paused state and paused time are saved in the history record, so a paused task can still be resumed after a restart.

**Where I went beyond the prompt, following the spec:** if a paused task's conversation can't be carried on, it resumes in a new conversation. That message includes its original prompt and its output so far, followed by the resume prompt. I also added the resume prompt to the settings window's injected prompts.

**Test fixes:**
- The new test and the existing `cancelling` test both start real harness runs. They failed in the full suite because neither called `allow_parking()`, which the other harness-run tests use; I added it to both.
- A finished run now drops its event stream straight away.
- I updated the system-prompt and settings tests for the new Resume prompt.

**Still failing, not caused by this change:**
- 13 compile and completion tests in `hidden_anchor`, `piton_lsp`, `project_lsp`, `file_view` and `chat_input` fail because your uncommitted spec edits renamed `ApplicationScope` to `Application`.
- `long_output_is_measured_a_few_rows_a_frame` fails sometimes when run with the other tests. It also failed with my test switched off, and passes on its own.
